subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit and implicit session resets, and should that contract live in core reset flow or in a memory/plugin lifecycle surface?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes hidden agent execution, transcript retention, reset latency, workspace writes, and possibly config/default behavior, so automation should not choose the security and product boundary.

options.title: Design a bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Add a core-owned or memory-plugin-owned pre-reset capability with explicit timeouts, sandbox/read-only guards, audit behavior, and coverage for explicit, daily, and idle resets.

options.title: Keep hook-based preservation only
options.body: Rely on session_end, before_reset, session-memory, and memory plugins for raw or external preservation, leaving agentic flushing to compaction and active turns.

options.title: Fold into broader reset lifecycle UX
options.body: Handle this as part of the larger reset-warning, opt-out, restore, and continuity product decision before adding hidden reset-time agent work.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned or memory-plugin-owned pre-reset capability with explicit timeouts, sandbox/read-only guards, audit behavior, and coverage for explicit, daily, and idle resets.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the original memory-flush implementation and the reset policy history, making him the best available owner for the cross-boundary decision.
